jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Lithuania governs AI through the Ministry of the Economy and Innovation's National AI Strategic Guidelines 2026-2035, which replaced the 2019 AI strategy, and a 2024 Seimas resolution on principles for AI use in the public sector, which ministries and agencies are turning into binding internal AI rules (interior, social security and labour, health, environment). A 2025 law makes the Innovation Agency the AI Act notifying authority and operator of an AI sandbox, while the main AI Act implementation bill, naming the communications regulator (RRT) as market surveillance authority, was still before the Seimas in October 2026. The Ombudsperson for Academic Ethics has issued ethical AI guidelines for research and studies.
lead_institutions: Ministry of the Economy and Innovation
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Government and regulator websites blocked access, so the reviewer used the parliament's legal register; the AI Act implementation bill is still before the Seimas and is listed as a lead, and two records could only be located.

instruments.official_title: Dėl 2026–2035 metų nacionalinių dirbtinio intelekto strateginių gairių patvirtinimo
instruments.english_title: Order No. 4-156 on approval of the 2026-2035 National Artificial Intelligence Strategic Guidelines
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of the Economy and Innovation of the Republic of Lithuania
instruments.current_status: Adopted 20 April 2026, published in the Register of Legal Acts (TAR) on 20 April 2026 under No. 2026-06332, and in force 21 April 2026. The order itself carries the date and number, although the attached PDF's approval stamp leaves the date blank.
instruments.summary: Order No. 4-156 of the Minister of the Economy and Innovation (20 April 2026) approves Lithuania's 2026-2035 National AI Strategic Guidelines, prepared with the Innovation Agency and the State Digital Solutions Agency. The guidelines set four directions (AI empowering people; secure infrastructure and data; AI for society, including an AI-first principle and AI procurement in the public sector; AI as an economic engine, including a clear AI regulatory framework) with indicators, and the Ministry monitors implementation and reviews indicators at least every two years. An annex sets out the national AI governance scheme: the Innovation Agency as AI Act notifying authority and business AI sandbox, the Communications Regulatory Authority (RRT) as main market surveillance authority alongside the Bank of Lithuania, the State Data Protection Inspectorate and sector bodies, and the GovAI competence centre for the public sector.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; it follows the unapproved 2019 strategy and 2022 action plan and sets the planned AI Act governance model.
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of the Economy and Innovation of the Republic of Lithuania

instruments.official_title: Dėl dirbtinio intelekto technologijų naudojimo viešajame sektoriuje principų
instruments.english_title: Seimas Resolution No. XIV-2620 on the principles of use of artificial intelligence technologies in the public sector
instruments.issuing_authority: Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania
instruments.current_status: Adopted 9 May 2024 (No. XIV-2620), published in TAR 16 May 2024 No. 2024-08947. A resolution addressed to the Government; it does not itself impose legal obligations.
instruments.summary: Seimas resolution of 9 May 2024 calling on the Government to ensure that public-sector bodies using AI follow eleven principles, including human control and review of AI-based administrative decisions, responsibility for outcomes, traceability of AI's influence on results, equal treatment, use only for lawful purposes, and continuous public disclosure of the AI technologies used. It defines the public sector broadly (budgetary and public institutions, state and municipal enterprises, regional development councils) and refers to the EU AI Act.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Parliamentary principles for public-sector AI; cited as the basis for ministry and agency AI rules (Interior, Social Security and Labour, Environmental Protection Agency).

instruments.issuing_authority: Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania
instruments.current_status: Adopted 14 January 2025, published in TAR 22 January 2025 No. 2025-00715; in force 1 April 2025, with Art. 5(4) (notifying authority) from 2 August 2025 and Art. 5(5) (AI sandbox) from 1 January 2026. The Communications Regulatory Authority's AI sandbox page identifies the implementing institution as the Innovation Agency (Inovacijų agentūra). The Government-submitted package of 27 May 2026 (bill XVP-1564) would amend Articles 1, 2 and 14 again (see leads).
instruments.summary: Amends the Law on Technologies and Innovation to implement parts of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), which it lists in a new annex of implemented EU acts. It assigns the state technology and innovation policy implementing institution the functions of AI Act notifying authority (Art. 28(1) and 70(1)), applying procedures set by the Minister of the Economy and Innovation, and requires it to set up and supervise an AI regulatory sandbox under Art. 57(1). The law entered into force on 1 April 2025; the notifying-authority provision applies from 2 August 2025 and the sandbox provision from 1 January 2026.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First Lithuanian statute implementing the EU AI Act (notifying authority and AI regulatory sandbox).

instruments.official_title: Dėl Dirbtinio intelekto sistemų naudojimo Lietuvos Respublikos vidaus reikalų ministerijoje tvarkos aprašo patvirtinimo
instruments.english_title: Order No. 1V-298 approving the Procedure for the use of artificial intelligence systems in the Ministry of the Interior
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Lithuania
instruments.current_status: Adopted 8 April 2026, published in TAR 8 April 2026 No. 2026-05747, in force 9 April 2026. Binding on Ministry of the Interior staff.
instruments.summary: Minister of the Interior order of 8 April 2026, citing Seimas Resolution XIV-2620, setting principles, conditions and responsibilities for AI system use by Ministry of the Interior staff. Use requires an appointed AI officer and AI systems administrator, an impact assessment before any new AI system is used, an approved list of permitted AI systems, individual permissions recorded in an AI use register, and procedures for monitoring, inventory, review, audit and incident management; discriminatory AI-generated content may not be used.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ministry-level binding internal rules for AI use, implementing the Seimas public-sector AI principles.

instruments.english_title: Order No. A1-51 approving the Rules on the application of artificial intelligence in the activities of the Ministry of Social Security and Labour
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Social Security and Labour of the Republic of Lithuania
instruments.current_status: Adopted 22 January 2026, published in TAR 22 January 2026 No. 2026-00877. The order originally entered into force 1 March 2026; its entry into force was changed by order A1-402 of 30 June 2026 and the register lists the current version as in force from 2 August 2026 (points 2 and 3 from 23 January 2026). Also amended by order A1-127 of 26 February 2026.
instruments.summary: Minister of Social Security and Labour order of 22 January 2026, citing Seimas Resolution XIV-2620, setting principles and rules for responsible AI use in the Ministry and recommending them to its subordinate institutions. The rules require a list of approved AI systems (with impact and data protection assessments), forbid unlisted or personal AI accounts and uploading personal data or classified information, assign an AI officer, and cover risk management, transparency and logging, AI procurement, monitoring and information security.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ministry-level binding internal AI rules covering risk, transparency and procurement.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Health of the Republic of Lithuania
instruments.current_status: Adopted 10 June 2026, published in TAR 10 June 2026 No. 2026-10206, in force 11 June 2026.
instruments.summary: Minister of Health order of 10 June 2026 approving guidelines that set principles, an objective, directions, tasks and actions for AI development in Lithuania's health system to 2031. The first direction aims to build the legal, organisational and technological basis for developing, testing, deploying and evaluating AI in health, including a national health data architecture and common clinical data model based on international standards and integration with the European Health Data Space.

instruments.english_title: Order No. AV-102 approving the Rules on the use of artificial intelligence in the activities of the Environmental Protection Agency
instruments.current_status: Adopted 4 June 2026, published in TAR 4 June 2026 No. 2026-09835; in force 3 August 2026. Amended by order AV-109 of 10 June 2026.
instruments.summary: Director's order of 4 June 2026 implementing the EU AI Act and GDPR and citing Seimas Resolution XIV-2620, setting rules for AI use across the agency's activities. It covers risk management, transparency (documenting each AI use's purpose, training data, models, versions, tests and impact assessments, and giving affected persons information on request), AI procurement contract terms (e.g. suppliers may not use agency data to train their own models without written permission), monitoring, information security and responsibilities.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Agency-level binding AI rules, including AI procurement clauses and a right to information for affected persons.

instruments.current_status: Approved 29 April 2024, published in TAR 30 April 2024 No. 2024-07913, in force 1 May 2024. Recommendations to research and study institutions.
instruments.summary: Guidelines of the Ombudsperson for Academic Ethics and Procedures (29 April 2024) giving universities, colleges, research institutes and the academic community recommendations on ethical use of AI, including generative AI, in studies and research. They set general ethical principles and address open science, publication ethics, intellectual property, institution-level policies and evaluation and validation of AI tools, and recommend that institutions adopt their own AI ethics guidelines.

instruments.current_status: Adopted 11 June 1996 (published Valstybės žinios 1996-07-03, No. 63-1479), with several new versions since; the register lists a current consolidated version from 30 June 2026.
instruments.summary: Lithuania's general personal data protection law (No. I-1374), which governs the processing of personal data, including for training and using AI systems, alongside the GDPR. The State Data Protection Inspectorate is the supervisory authority, as Lithuania declared when ratifying the Protocol amending Convention 108 (Law XIII-2499 of 2019).
